scales.heading: {{key}} {{scale}}
scales.intro: Every note of the scale across the neck. The pulsing ring marks the lowest root — the best place to start.

descriptions.major: The reference scale of Western music: bright and stable.
descriptions.minor: Same notes as the Aeolian mode: dark and melancholic.
descriptions.ionian: 1st mode of the major scale — identical to the major scale.
descriptions.dorian: 2nd mode: minor with a raised 6th. A funk, jazz and Latin staple.
descriptions.phrygian: 3rd mode: minor with a flat 2nd. Spanish and metal flavor.
descriptions.lydian: 4th mode: major with a raised 4th. Dreamy and floating.
descriptions.mixolydian: 5th mode: major with a flat 7th. Blues, rock and funk over dominant chords.
descriptions.locrian: 7th mode: flat 2nd and flat 5th. Tense; used over half-diminished chords.

arpeggios.intro: Every chord tone across the neck. The pulsing ring marks the lowest root — the best place to start.

descriptions.maj: Root, major 3rd and 5th: the foundation of most bass lines.
descriptions.min: Root, minor 3rd and 5th: darker than major.
descriptions.dim: Two minor 3rds stacked: tense, it wants to resolve.
descriptions.aug: Two major 3rds stacked: unstable and dreamy.
descriptions.sus4: The 4th replaces the 3rd: open, neither major nor minor.
descriptions.maj7: Major triad plus the major 7th: the smooth sound of jazz ballads and soul.
descriptions.dom7: Major triad plus the flat 7th: blues, funk and every V chord.
descriptions.m7: Minor triad plus the flat 7th: the ii chord, and a funk and R&B staple.
descriptions.m7b5: Diminished triad plus the flat 7th: the ii chord in minor keys.
descriptions.dim7: Minor 3rds stacked all the way up: a passing chord full of tension.
descriptions.maj6: Major triad plus the 6th: classic swing and walking-bass color.
descriptions.m6: Minor triad plus the major 6th: a Latin and jazz minor sound.

ear.title: Ear Training
ear.description: Learn where every note lives on the neck, by name and by ear.
ear.prompt: Tap where this note is on the neck (frets 0–{{max}}). Press Hear it to listen first.
ear.promptHidden: Press Hear it, then tap the note you heard (frets 0–{{max}}).
ear.exact: Correct! The same note you heard, in the same octave.
ear.tappedHigher: Right note! The one you heard was an octave lower.
ear.tappedLower: Right note! The one you heard was an octave higher.
ear.wrong: Not quite: you tapped {{tapped}}. Every {{note}} is marked.
ear.fretboard: Bass neck: tap a fret to answer

player.hint: Tip: tap any fret to hear it.

metronome.title: Metronome
metronome.description: Keep steady time, read rhythms and train your inner clock.
metronome.cycleHint: Tap to change: accent → normal → silent
metronome.accentsHelp: Tap a beat to make it accented, normal or silent.
metronome.speedHelp: Raise (or lower) the tempo step by step up to a target.
metronome.gapHelp: Play some bars, then mute some: are you still on the beat when it comes back?
metronome.shortcuts: Shortcuts: Space start/stop · T tap tempo · ↑↓ tempo (Shift ×5)

tuner.title: Tuner
tuner.description: Play an open string and tune until the needle is centered. Tap a string to hear its pitch.
tuner.idle: Press Start, then play a string
tuner.playHint: Tap to hear this string's pitch
tuner.levelHint: If this bar barely moves when you play, move the bass closer to the microphone or check your input device.
tuner.privacy: Uses your microphone. Audio is analyzed on this device and never sent anywhere.

errors.denied: Microphone access was blocked. Allow it in your browser's site settings and try again.
errors.no-device: No microphone was found. Connect one and try again.
errors.unsupported: This browser can't use the microphone here. Try a recent Chrome, Firefox or Safari over HTTPS.
